Eyes in the Back of My Head
May the Force Be With You
You just signed with {club} and three agents want to run your career. Your offers, and how much of each paycheck you keep, depend on this.
More offers and bigger deals. Takes 10%.
You sign with an agency that moves half of basketball. Your phone never stops.
Your aunt, who has known you since mini-basketball
It stays in the family. You feel backed and grounded.
No commission, but clubs will scrutinise you.
You'll negotiate yourself. You save money, though offers will come in lower.
Your recent games caught the eye. Two brands want you wearing their shoes on court.
Your face goes up on a billboard downtown. Your friends keep sending you photos.
They design your own model and pay more.
They send sketches of "your" shoe. Small brand, but all yours.
If you keep producing, another offer will come… or not.

You sign. It's not a downtown billboard, but it's a start.
You decline. Time to prove on court you are worth more.

Party, press and social. You arrive just in time for warm-ups.
They sell out in two hours. The coach did not love you arriving at the last minute.
Something low-key at the neighbourhood store
You sign shoes for the neighbourhood kids. There are some tears, and not only theirs.
One year left on your deal
{club} wants to talk. If you do not sign, you will be a free agent this summer… or left without a team.

It may go great or break the relationship.
The club caves: you sign the deal of your life.
The front office walks out. Things turn sour.
You leave in summer. The club will not like it.
You announce you will not renew. Your minutes start to wobble.
Serious injury: how do you treat it?
Doctors confirm weeks out. There are several paths and none is perfect.
Surgery goes well. It will be long, but you will come back without fear.
You respond well and return ahead of schedule.
Relapse. This time it leaves a mark.
Expensive, but speeds the return safely.
You get treated at a top clinic. Shorter timeline, no risk.

You learn {opponent}'s help rotations by heart.
You arrive tired, but you know where everyone will be.
You sleep like a baby. The calm shows on your first shot.
Let your people live it with you.

May open a door… or close one.

Everyone is talking about your shot

{teammate} takes you to dinner. The locker room closes ranks.

Someone posts a photo at four in the morning.
Party videos arrive while you stretch. You sleep nine hours.
The photo from that night reaches a TV show. The club wants an explanation.

"It was a birthday, not a crime."
Your followers love it. The front office, not so much.
The shooting coach offers to stay with you every morning before practice.
Your mechanics improve. Your knees grumble a bit.
You gain free-throw confidence without wrecking yourself.

You will learn to read the game.
He teaches you tricks that are not in any video.

Talk to the coach about your role

"Minutes are earned in practice." The door closes.

You keep waiting. Sometimes the moment comes on its own.
A reporter says {club} is listening to offers for you. The locker room has read it.
"I'm happy here." Nobody knows if it is true, not even you.
Have your agent look into it

An emoji is worth a thousand words.

Your name on the rim forever.

You promise next year. They will remind you.

You say no. Months later you will see it on the news, for better or worse.
{teammate} wears the number you have always wanted. He may leave next year… or not.

You feel fine as you are.

The trainer wants you to rest

The league invites you to the All-Star weekend dunk contest.

You earn his respect and a fine.

Trick question at a press conference
